title: Lower abdominal pain in a 26-year-old graduate student
intended_learner: Medical students and first-year emergency medicine residents
unknown_response: I'm not sure. I can't really tell you anything about that.
prebrief: You are the emergency medicine resident. Hannah Lindqvist, 26, has had worsening lower abdominal pain since yesterday evening. Take a history, request the examination and tests you need, and decide on a disposition. She seems in a hurry to leave.

profile.name: Hannah Lindqvist
profile.background: Chemistry graduate student two days from her thesis defence; lives with a roommate.
profile.personality: Conscientious, anxious, tries to stay in control; honest when she feels heard.
profile.speech_style: Precise and quick, a little clipped when in pain.

differential: Ovarian torsion or ruptured ovarian cyst
Ectopic pregnancy (excluded by a negative test)
Urinary tract infection or kidney stone
teaching_points: Pain that starts around the navel and moves to the right lower abdomen, with loss of appetite, is a classic story for appendicitis.
Every woman of child-bearing age with abdominal pain needs a pregnancy test before imaging.
Ask why a patient waited: fear of an operation can drive a request to leave, and it is addressable.
Record the allergy before anyone prescribes an antibiotic.

facts.statement: Lower right abdominal pain since yesterday evening, getting worse
facts.patient_answer: My stomach has been hurting since last night, down on the right side, and it keeps getting worse.

facts.statement: Began about 18 hours ago as a dull ache around the navel, then moved to the right lower abdomen overnight
facts.patient_answer: It started yesterday evening as a dull ache around my belly button. Overnight it moved down to the right.

facts.statement: Now sharp and constant, 7/10
facts.patient_answer: It's sharp now, and it doesn't let up. About a seven out of ten.

facts.statement: Worse with walking, coughing and bumps in the car; best lying still with knees bent
facts.patient_answer: Walking and coughing make it much worse. Every bump on the drive here hurt. Lying still with my knees up is the only thing that helps.

facts.statement: No appetite since yesterday; nauseated; vomited once this morning
facts.patient_answer: I haven't wanted to eat since yesterday. I feel sick, and I threw up once this morning.

facts.statement: Felt hot and shivery overnight; did not take her temperature
facts.patient_answer: I felt hot and shivery last night. I didn't take my temperature.

facts.statement: Last bowel movement yesterday, normal; no diarrhoea, no blood
facts.patient_answer: I went yesterday and it was normal. No diarrhea, no blood.

facts.statement: No burning, frequency or blood in urine
facts.patient_answer: No, peeing is normal. No burning, no blood.

facts.statement: Last period three weeks ago and normal; no vaginal bleeding or discharge
facts.patient_answer: My last period was three weeks ago, right on time and normal. No bleeding or discharge since.

facts.statement: Sexually active with one male partner; uses a combined oral contraceptive pill, missed no pills this month
facts.patient_answer: I have one partner, my boyfriend. I'm on the pill and I haven't missed any this month.

facts.statement: No chronic medical conditions; no previous surgery; appendix in place
facts.patient_answer: I'm healthy. No medical problems, and I've never had an operation.

facts.statement: Combined oral contraceptive daily; took ibuprofen 400 mg at 6 am with little relief
facts.patient_answer: Just my birth control pill. I took an ibuprofen, 400 milligrams, at six this morning. It barely touched it.

facts.statement: Penicillin allergy: widespread hives and lip swelling at age 12
facts.patient_answer: I'm allergic to penicillin. I got hives all over and my lips swelled when I was twelve.

facts.statement: Last ate at about 7 pm yesterday; sips of water at 5 am
facts.patient_answer: I last ate around seven last night. I've only had sips of water since, at about five.

facts.statement: No family history of bowel disease; father has high blood pressure
facts.patient_answer: Nothing with the stomach or bowels in my family. My dad has high blood pressure.

facts.statement: Does not smoke; a glass of wine at weekends; no recreational drugs
facts.patient_answer: I don't smoke. A glass of wine on weekends. No drugs.

facts.statement: Graduate student in chemistry; defends her thesis in two days
facts.patient_answer: I'm a grad student in chemistry. I defend my thesis in two days.

facts.statement: Lives with a roommate; parents live four hours away
facts.patient_answer: I live with a roommate. My parents are about four hours away.

facts.statement: Waited 18 hours before coming in and wants to leave quickly because she fears an operation: her mother was very unwell after a general anaesthetic, and the thesis defence is in two days
facts.patient_answer: The truth is I waited because I'm terrified you'll say I need surgery. My mom was really sick after an anesthetic, she took hours to wake up properly. And my defense is in two days. I can't miss it.
facts.cover_answer: I just need something for the pain so I can get back to my work.

facts.statement: Temperature 38.1 C
facts.label: Temperature

facts.statement: Heart rate 104 beats/min
facts.label: Heart rate

facts.statement: Blood pressure 118/72 mmHg, respiratory rate 18/min, SpO2 99% on room air
Abdomen: tender in the right lower quadrant with guarding and rebound tenderness; pressing on the left lower abdomen causes pain on the right; bowel sounds reduced
Urine pregnancy test negative
facts.label: Urine hCG

facts.statement: White blood cell count 14.8 x10^3/mcL (reference 4.5-11.0)
facts.label: WBC

facts.statement: C-reactive protein 6.2 mg/dL (healthy adults usually below 0.3)
facts.label: CRP

facts.statement: Urinalysis: no nitrites, no white cells, no blood
CT abdomen and pelvis: dilated appendix (11 mm) with wall thickening and surrounding fat stranding; no abscess, no free air

artifacts.title: Triage note
artifacts.content: 26-year-old woman, walked in bent forward holding her right side. Lower abdominal pain since yesterday evening. Vomited once. Asked twice how long this will take. ESI 3.

artifacts.title: Blood count
artifacts.interpretation: Raised white cell count, in keeping with an inflammatory or infective process. Not specific.

artifacts.title: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast (report)
artifacts.content: Technique: CT of the abdomen and pelvis with intravenous contrast. Findings: the appendix measures 11 mm in diameter with wall thickening and stranding of the surrounding fat. No appendicolith. No abscess or free intraperitoneal air. Ovaries and uterus unremarkable. No hydronephrosis.
artifacts.interpretation: Findings consistent with acute uncomplicated appendicitis: surgical review. Note the penicillin allergy when antibiotics are chosen.

artifacts.title: Student health clinic note (4 months ago)
artifacts.content: Routine visit for contraception review. Well. Blood pressure 112/70. Combined oral contraceptive continued. Allergy recorded: penicillin (hives, lip swelling, childhood). No other medicines.
artifacts.interpretation: Confirms the penicillin allergy and the contraceptive pill.

objectives.criterion: Elicits the migration of the pain, what worsens it, and the loss of appetite and nausea
objectives.evidence_rule: met when all three are elicited
objectives.feedback_missed: Ask where the pain started and whether it moved, what makes it worse, and about appetite.

objectives.criterion: Takes a menstrual and sexual history and requests a pregnancy test
objectives.evidence_rule: met when the last period and sexual history are asked and a pregnancy test is requested
objectives.feedback_missed: Lower abdominal pain in a 26-year-old woman: ask about her last period and contraception, and test for pregnancy before imaging.

objectives.criterion: Identifies the penicillin allergy and the reaction
objectives.evidence_rule: met when the allergy is elicited
objectives.feedback_missed: Always ask about allergies and what the reaction was.

objectives.criterion: Examines the abdomen and requests a blood count and appropriate imaging
objectives.evidence_rule: met when all three are requested

objectives.criterion: Finds out why she waited and why she wants to leave
objectives.evidence_rule: the patient shares her fear of surgery after the learner acknowledges her worry
objectives.feedback_met: You slowed down, acknowledged the pressure she is under, and she told you what was really worrying her.
objectives.feedback_missed: She keeps asking to leave. Acknowledge the pressure of the thesis defence, then ask what worries her about being here.

objectives.criterion: Runs a structured interview: introduction, open question first, summary, clear close
objectives.evidence_rule: three of: introduction, early open question, summary, closing

objectives.criterion: Recognises probable appendicitis and arranges surgical review rather than discharge
objectives.evidence_rule: disposition is admit, with a summary naming the examination or CT findings
